output.summary: KEP-5067 adds a status.observedGeneration field to pod status, reusing metadata.generation, so the pod status can express which pod spec update the writer (kubelet) has reflected. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale:
The ResizeStatus race between API server and Kubelet left a gap in knowing whether the latest resize was acknowledged by the Kubelet. The KEP addresses this generically for any pod update by leveraging metadata.generation and a new status.observedGeneration field. ObservedGeneration was preferred over copying the desired resources or whole podspec into status because it is more concise and consistent with resources like StatefulSet.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Add a 'desired resources' field to status, or an 'observed spec' field that copies the whole podspec into status
alternatives.why_not: ObservedGeneration expresses the same amount of information while being significantly more concise, and is consistent with other resources such as StatefulSet.

alternatives.option: Bump generation only when a downward API referenced field changes (sftim suggestion)
alternatives.why_not: Offered as an optional alternative in review discussion; the sources do not record a decision against it beyond the KEP's chosen generation-based approach.

evidence.quote: The idea is to leverage the existing `metadata.generation` field and add a new `status.observedGeneration` field to the pod status.
ObservedGeneration is preferable over these alternatives because it expresses the same amount of inforrmation while being significantly more concise
the singular status.observedGeneration field in the pod status means only a single writer can set it.
I think a reasonable path in the kubelet here is to use feature enabled || pod status has non-zero observedGeneration to decide whether to propagate metadata.generation to status.observedGeneration.
